**CI checks (must pass before merge):**

- [ ] `forbidden-patterns` — the same check `sepac check` ran on the QA host
- [ ] `compiled-policy` — Stream 9 `validate_policy_semantics.sh` for myapp, shopapi, and payments
- [ ] `version-consistency`

A laptop without `selinux-policy-devel` does not compile. The Stream 9 job does.

### 6. Security and Sysadmin Checklist (Admin Team Review)

> Full principles and anti-patterns: [`docs/guides/201-TOOL-COMMANDS.md`](../../docs/guides/201-TOOL-COMMANDS.md#what-a-pull-request-must-not-contain) (what a pull request must not contain).

| Security Check | Status | Notes / Approver Initials |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **No Over-Permissive Grants** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | CI `forbidden-patterns`; no `shadow_t`, `unconfined_t`, `sysadm_t`, or broad `var_t:file write` |
| **Custom Labels Enforced** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | FHS paths `/var/lib/myapp`, `/var/log/myapp`, `/run/myapp`; dedicated types; `.fc` without `--` on dirs |
| **Port Assignments Validated** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | `myapp_port_t` TCP 8888, `myapp_backend_port_t` TCP 8889 (not blanket `unreserved_port_t`) |
| **Compilation Test** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | `sepac check APP` on the QA host, and CI `compiled-policy` |
| **Path Labeling (restorecon -n)** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | The canary's label check passes; `sepac status APP` shows `Labels ok` |
| **Domain Context Verified** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | Deploy report shows `myapp.service` → `myapp_t`, backend → `myapp_backend_t` |
| **Soak Period (7–14 days)** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | `sepac soak` (AAP **Soak monitor**) daily — net-new vs installed policy; `sepac soak --status` before enforce |
| **Systemd-Only Restart** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | Service started via `systemctl restart`, not manual `python app.py` |
| **Prod Canary Host** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | `sepac canary --env production --limit canary` before fleet enforce |
| **Canary Readiness** | ⬜ Pass / ⬜ Reject | Plan to run `sepac canary` before production enforce |

### 7. Admin Action

**After merge:** `sepac build && sepac publish`, then `sepac canary` (AAP **SELinux – Release canary**).

**Soak:** `sepac soak` daily (AAP **SELinux – Soak monitor**): zero **net-new** access against the installed policy. Before enforce: `sepac soak --status`. If the soak fails: [`docs/shipping.md#a-denial-after-ship`](../../docs/shipping.md#a-denial-after-ship) (a new pull request and a recanary, not a live patch).

**Production enforce:** `sepac enforce --ticket CHG…` (AAP workflow **SELinux – Promote to enforce**) after the soak. See [`docs/shipping.md`](../../docs/shipping.md) and [`ansible/aap/`](../../ansible/aap/).

```bash
sepac canary  --env production --limit canary
sepac soak    --env production --limit canary
sepac soak    --env production --limit canary --status
sepac enforce --env production --limit canary --ticket CHG123
```

**Rollback:** `sepac rollback --env production`
